headline: PM asks Banglalink to make smartphones and internet more affordable
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged the telecom operator to reduce prices to ensure digital services are accessible to people from all walks of life.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has asked Banglalink authorities to take steps to make smartphones more affordable and further reduce internet prices.
The request was made during a meeting with Augie Fabela, chairman of VEON, the parent company of Banglalink, at the Prime Minister's Office in the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.
The Prime Minister urged the company to ensure that people from all sections of society can own smartphones and access digital services more easily.
The meeting focused on expanding digital accessibility across the country to bridge the digital divide.
Also present were the Minister for Post, Telecommunications, Information Technology and Science and Technology, and the Prime Minister's Adviser on the same portfolio.
Banglalink CEO Johan Hendrik Martinus Buse and VEON Board Member Michiel Soeting were also part of the delegation.
caption:
Will internet and smartphones become cheaper? The Prime Minister has urged Banglalink to lower prices for all.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has asked Banglalink authorities to take steps to make smartphones more affordable and further reduce internet prices.

The request was made during a meeting with Augie Fabela, chairman of VEON, the parent company of Banglalink, at the Prime Minister's Office in the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.

The Prime Minister urged the company to ensure that people from all sections of society can own smartphones and access digital services more easily.

The meeting focused on expanding digital accessibility across the country to bridge the digital divide.

Also present were the Minister for Post, Telecommunications, Information Technology and Science and Technology, and the Prime Minister's Adviser on the same portfolio.

Banglalink CEO Johan Hendrik Martinus Buse and VEON Board Member Michiel Soeting were also part of the delegation.

headline_marked: Ekushey Padak winner [[Artist Mustafa Monwar passes away]] at 91
headline: Ekushey Padak winner Artist Mustafa Monwar passes away at 91
summary: The 'Puppet Man of Bangladesh' died on Monday morning at Square Hospital in Dhaka after battling age-related illnesses and pneumonia.
details: Mustafa Monwar, a pioneering artist, theatre director, and art researcher, passed away at around 8:30 am on Monday at Square Hospital in Dhaka.
The renowned artist was 91 years old. He had been battling various age-related illnesses and was admitted to the hospital on June 14 after contracting pneumonia.
Monwar was born on September 1, 1935, in Jashore's Sreepur. He graduated top of his class in Fine Arts from the Kolkata College of Arts and Crafts in 1959.
Known as the 'Puppet Man of Bangladesh', he made significant contributions to puppetry, painting, and theatre directing.
Throughout his career, he served in several high-profile roles, including Director General of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy and Managing Director of the Bangladesh Film Development Corporation (FDC).
He was honored with the Ekushey Padak in 2004 and received numerous other awards, including the Tenashinas Padak and the Bangladesh Charushilpali Sangsad Award.
He is survived by his wife, Mary Monwar, and two children, a son and a daughter.
caption:
The 'Puppet Man of Bangladesh' is no more. Mustafa Monwar, a cultural icon and Ekushey Padak winner, has passed away at 91.

Mustafa Monwar, a pioneering artist, theatre director, and art researcher, passed away at around 8:30 am on Monday at Square Hospital in Dhaka.

The renowned artist was 91 years old. He had been battling various age-related illnesses and was admitted to the hospital on June 14 after contracting pneumonia.

Monwar was born on September 1, 1935, in Jashore's Sreepur. He graduated top of his class in Fine Arts from the Kolkata College of Arts and Crafts in 1959.

Known as the 'Puppet Man of Bangladesh', he made significant contributions to puppetry, painting, and theatre directing.

Throughout his career, he served in several high-profile roles, including Director General of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy and Managing Director of the Bangladesh Film Development Corporation (FDC).

He was honored with the Ekushey Padak in 2004 and received numerous other awards, including the Tenashinas Padak and the Bangladesh Charushilpali Sangsad Award.

He is survived by his wife, Mary Monwar, and two children, a son and a daughter.
